chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop - Customizing Fabric Tape Pull Tabs
chunks.content: ## Overview of Customizing Fabric Tape Pull Tabs in CLO This section explains the step-by-step process of creating and customizing a self-designed cloth zipper pull tab in CLO, including importing zipper components, defining positions, adjusting sizes, simulating cloth panels, applying fabrics and stickers, and exporting the final OBJ file for integration. --- ## Importing and Setting Up the Zipper Component This section covers how to import a zipper OBJ component into CLO, adjust its size, and correctly position it using coordinate points to ensure accurate alignment. - Open the drawer window and navigate to the zipper component section. - Locate and double-click the desired zipper OBJ file to add it into the workspace. - Confirm the unit of measurement is set to millimeters (mm). - Imported zippers may be scaled 10 times larger than the original size for packaging purposes; adjust this scale accordingly. - Once added, close the drawer window to view the zipper in the 3D workspace. - Align the zipper's self-defined position to the coordinate point for accurate placement. - You can move the zipper down slightly, even below the ground level, to simulate realistic placement. - Use the 3D window’s simulation attributes (accessed via the arrow in the blank area and ground triangle) to simulate the ground surface. - Freeze the zipper component to lock its position and prevent unintended movement. - To resize the zipper, select it in the object window, unlock the fixed ratio if needed, and adjust the size values in the attribute editor. Reposition as necessary. --- ## Creating and Simulating a Cloth Panel on the Zipper This section details how to create a cloth panel that attaches to the zipper, including shape creation, sewing line editing, and simulation setup. - Use the shape tool in the 2D window to create a rectangular cloth panel narrower than the zipper’s top width. For example, if the zipper is 60 mm wide, create a panel 40 mm wide and 200 mm tall. - Position the panel near the zipper using the positioning ball, preferably in the world coordinate system to maintain consistent placement regardless of view. - Split the panel into two parts in the 3D window to facilitate detailed sewing. - Use the editor sewing line tool to keep only the sewing lines at the top and bottom edges. - Set particle diameter to 5 and collision thickness to 1 in the cloth panel properties. - Enable simulation to see the cloth naturally drape over the zipper. - To make the panel flatter, add internal sewing lines near areas where the cloth needs restriction: - Click in the 3D window to add sewing lines at key points (identified by small blue dots). - Use the sewing line tool to join sections, then set these sewing lines to the overlay type. - After sewing, simulate again to observe cloth behavior. - Adjust the panel length as needed by stretching the bottom edge; minor collisions can be resolved by adjusting layer settings.

chunks.content: - To make the panel flatter, add internal sewing lines near areas where the cloth needs restriction: - Click in the 3D window to add sewing lines at key points (identified by small blue dots). - Use the sewing line tool to join sections, then set these sewing lines to the overlay type. - After sewing, simulate again to observe cloth behavior. - Adjust the panel length as needed by stretching the bottom edge; minor collisions can be resolved by adjusting layer settings. - Raise corners to create diagonal angles, e.g., move a corner up by 20 mm. --- ## Applying Fabrics and Stickers to the Cloth Panel This section explains how to assign fabric textures and add stickers or decals to the cloth panel for realistic visual effects. - Open the fabric library, search for the desired fabric, and drag it onto the cloth panel to apply texture. - The fabric properties can make the cloth stiffer or softer; view changes in the thick texture surface mode. - To add stickers: - Right-click the chosen sticker in the library and add it as a sticker. - Place the sticker on the 2D cloth panel and resize as needed. - Stickers have locked aspect ratios and positions to prevent distortion; replacing textures requires attention to ratio and alignment. - Colors and textures can be changed independently. - Texture image ratios can be adjusted numerically (e.g., enlarging from 10 to 11) to better fit the panel. - Adjust texture strength to enhance visibility of text or logos on the sticker. - Adding additional layers or texture height adjustments is possible for complex designs. --- ## Exporting the Customized Pull Tab as OBJ This section provides instructions for exporting the finished zipper pull tab, including file naming, export options, and unit scale considerations. - Use File > Export OBJ to open the export dialog. - Select the destination folder and name the file appropriately. - In export options: - Select to export all panels, stickers, and accessories. - Enable multiple targets if necessary. - Set the unit scale to centimeters (cm) for consistency. - Save as a compressed zip file. - Uncheck unnecessary options (three specific options should remain off; only the main export option is checked). - After export, locate and unzip the saved file folder. - The project file inside allows for future edits. - Important: Adjust the scale to 10% when returning from mm to cm to avoid oversized slices, as original scaling increased size by a factor of 10. - Preview the OBJ file in the import dialog to verify correctness before applying. --- ## Applying and Editing the Pull Tab in CLO Costumes This section explains how to apply the exported zipper pull tab to a costume, locate it correctly, and edit its materials and textures. - Open the costume with a 3D zipper model. - Apply the exported pull tab OBJ slice by selecting the appropriate triangle selector in the costume’s item list.

chunks.content: - Preview the OBJ file in the import dialog to verify correctness before applying. --- ## Applying and Editing the Pull Tab in CLO Costumes This section explains how to apply the exported zipper pull tab to a costume, locate it correctly, and edit its materials and textures. - Open the costume with a 3D zipper model. - Apply the exported pull tab OBJ slice by selecting the appropriate triangle selector in the costume’s item list. - Position the pull tab correctly on the garment. - To edit materials: - Select the entire zipper head and mouth for global edits. - Select individual zipper components for detailed customizations, such as the cloth bag or sticker. - Replace sticker textures by selecting the sticker position; ensure the replacement image matches the original ratio to avoid deformation. - Change colors or remove textures as needed. - Adjust texture image scale and strength for optimal appearance. - When adding layers or modifying texture height, save your work regularly. - Saved custom pull tabs can be reloaded and swapped as desired within the project. --- ## Summary This guide provides a detailed workflow for customizing fabric tape pull tabs in CLO, covering zipper import, cloth panel creation, fabric and sticker application, OBJ export, and integration into costumes. Attention to scale, alignment, and texture ratios is critical for accurate and visually appealing results.
